_meta.indication: MARGENZA is indicated, in combination with chemotherapy, for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2 regimens, at least one of which was for metastatic disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (1:1), open-label, active-controlled trial of margetuximab plus chemotherapy versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who had received prior treatment with other anti-HER2 therapies.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sequential primary endpoints of progression-free survival (PFS) by BICR, followed by overall survival (OS).
pivotal_trials.n: 536 patients randomized 1:1 (margetuximab plus chemotherapy n=266; trastuzumab plus chemotherapy n=270).
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 5.8 months (95% CI 5.5, 7.0) vs 4.9 months (95% CI 4.2, 5.6); stratified HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.59, 0.98); p=0.033. OS immature: median 21.6 vs 19.8 months (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.69, 1.13; p=0.2086). ORR 22% vs 16%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were fatigue/asthenia, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, headache, pyrexia, alopecia, abdominal pain, peripheral neuropathy, arthralgia/myalgia, cough, decreased appetite, dyspnea, infusion-related reactions, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, and extremity pain. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 16% of margetuximab-plus-chemotherapy patients. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1.1%. Left ventricular dysfunction occurred in 1.9%; infusion-related reactions in 13%.
target_moa: Margetuximab-cmkb, a HER2/neu receptor antagonist, is a chimeric Fc-engineered IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular domain of HER2, inhibits tumor cell proliferation, reduces shedding of the HER2 extracellular domain, and mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).
modality: mAb (chimeric Fc-engineered IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed Warning for Left Ventricular Dysfunction (MARGENZA may lead to reductions in LVEF) and Embryo-Fetal Toxicity (exposure during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm).

companion_dx_detail: The Applicant did not propose the use of a companion diagnostic or an FDA-approved test to select patients with HER2+ breast cancer.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic.

description.text: Labeling update to reflect final overall survival results of the SOPHIA trial

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a labeling revision to update the U.S. Prescribing Information (USPI) to reflect the final overall survival results of the SOPHIA trial (Study CP-MGAH22-04).

basis.text: Fast Track designation granted 12-Jan-2018 for treatment of patients with metastatic or locally advanced HER2-positive breast cancer previously treated with anti-HER2-targeted therapy.

summary.text: BLA 761150 was submitted under section 351(a) and received a Standard review; the product had Fast Track designation. It was approved December 2020 based on a statistically significant PFS improvement in the pivotal Phase 3 SOPHIA trial (regular approval, not accelerated approval).
